analyses.rationale: F33.1 (major depressive disorder, recurrent, moderate) describes an ACTIVE condition. The note documents resolution, not active illness: a bereavement-related episode treated ~3 years ago, sertraline discontinued 18 months ago, no recurrence, PHQ-9 of 1/27 (minimal), a normal psychiatric exam, and an explicit plan of 'No current treatment indicated.' A note-only coding expert would code remission (F33.42), not the active moderate code. F33.1 is an unsupported, high-value HCC (V28 HCC 155) diagnosis pad.

legal_brief: The documented encounter supports a Medicare Annual Wellness Visit, essential hypertension, hyperlipidemia, and osteopenia. The billed diagnosis F33.1 (major depressive disorder, recurrent, moderate) is contradicted by the note, which documents the depression as resolved: a bereavement-related episode treated approximately three years ago, sertraline discontinued 18 months ago, no recurrence, PHQ-9 of 1/27, a normal psychiatric exam, and an explicit plan of 'No current treatment indicated.' A note-only coding expert would code remission (F33.42), not the active moderate code. Billing F33.1 submits a high-value HCC diagnosis (V28 HCC 155, coefficient 0.299) the encounter does not support, inflating the Medicare Advantage risk score and capitated payment. Fraud type: dx_inflation. Verdict: fraud.
